items.detail: world/site (served at :8790/lumi/) is the blog, not a separate world/blog. One post per thing Lumi made or film it released, newest first, each in Lumi's voice with its verdict (how it came out, what works, what does not, next time), pictures and videos; index.html lists them. An RSS feed (world/site/feed.xml) that a reader can follow. Each release offers its world state (the snapshot it was made from) and the replay to download, so others can continue the game. Static files only (plain HTML or Bonito's static export), so it can later go public as it is. done_when: feed.xml validates, three posts with media, a download link that loads in NG.Game. Media: every post's pictures are path traced stills from the worker (`submit_job(:trace; ...)`, denoised with OIDN by default, 64+ samples, the same camera as the moment the post is about), its videos path traced films (denoised, 32+ samples a frame); raster screenshots only as quick previews while a render runs, swapped out when it is back. The human: "shouldn't the blog post raytraced videos or pictures with high spp?"

items.detail: Reproducible at daytime 0.99 (everyone asleep, Lumi's goal :sleep before the game): live_tests('Firefly catch: start') fails 'Lumi did not walk on W', although the W key lights up and state is :playing. move_heading!(Lumi, w, yaw, 0.1) called directly moves it 0.11 m, and the spot is on land. So the cause is between keys_down and JumpIn.step! inside FireflyCatch.step! (or something moving Lumi back each frame). Firefly catch is THE night game: a player at night cannot play it. done_when: the test passes at night, a night screenshot of Lumi walking in the game. Session 24 probe: in one live_eval (start_minigame!, state=:playing, push w into keys_down, invokelatest step!(m, game, 0.1)) Lumi DOES move 0.11 m, and step!(m.jump) again 0.11 m. So the game step works; over real frames something undoes it or keys_down loses w between frames at night: next, log c.pos each frame (frame!: sim -> systems -> minigame) for 10 frames with w held, and look at Separation and the sleep pile near Lumi's bed (Hopscotch walks there).
items.result: Cause: at night Lumi sleeps at (9.16, 2.38), wedged between a tree (8.46, 2.65) and a bush (9.61, 3.30), facing the bush; the Separation system pushes it out of the bush every frame, so W did nothing (reproduced: 6 frames, position unchanged, action :walk). Fix in plugins/firefly_catch.jl: reset! calls face_open!, which turns Lumi towards the most open direction (water and the Separation solids, 24 headings) when less than 1.5 m is free ahead. From that spot: yaw 1.28 -> 4.95, 1.4 m walked in 1.2 s; test 'Firefly catch: start card...' passes from the spot at night (it failed there before). media/firefly-night-walk.png (start card still up only because the state was set by hand).
items.title: Firefly catch at night: W does not walk Lumi

items.result:
Scoped in session 28: run_job(::Val{:trace}) (assets.jl:163) calls screenshot(path, w) (render.jl:128), which builds stage_scene + Stage(scene, w) from the snapshot only. Plugins draw into game.stage.scene from start!/step! with a Game (flora.jl variety_plot!, lamplight, moon, berry basket, ...), so nothing of theirs exists in the worker. Plan: in the worker build a headless Game around the snapshot (Game(root) + its stage on a stage_scene of the wanted size + load_plugins + start! every system and one step!), then trace that stage's scene with the RayMakie.Screen(rasterize = false). Same path later for movie frames (goal 2). Check: a trace shows the generated trees and flowers (compare with progress/session-0027/overview.png).
Fixed in the engine (session 28): new NG.game_still(path; root, size, samples) in render.jl builds a quiet copy of the game (Game(root; quiet = true): latest snapshot, every plugin loaded, no game_start event), a stage on a 3D scene that is a child of a root scene (so plugins get their 2D overlay, hidden for the still), starts and steps the systems 3 frames, syncs actors, then path traces with RayMakie. The worker's :trace job uses it by default (params "plugins" => false gives the old engine-only scene).
Evidence: media/s28/trace-plugins-mine2.png (960x540, 32 spp, 64 s): generated textured trees, flowers, Gloop's glass body, the stars; media/s28/trace-plugins-mine.png: pier, dirt path, lily pond, glowing night flowers. Before: media/s27-trace-flowers.png (sphere trees, stick flowers).
Note: the worker process has no Revise: it runs game_still after its next restart (the first test job 20261123-045332-824-trace still drew the old scene). Camera framing of traced stills belongs to the movie work (#80/#119).

items.result: Session 38: found the cause: not the sea (hiding sea and seabed live left the band, media/s38/hz-nosea.png, hz-nobed.png) but the sky. SunSkyLight had ground_enabled = false, so below the horizon the baked sky map is black, and the map is octahedral: the horizon runs diagonally through its texels and the black edge was drawn as a sawtooth. Now the sky's ground is a soft sea haze (scenery.jl SKY_GROUND = RGBf(0.45, 0.55, 0.65), stage_lights; set live). Before/after from the same camera: media/s38/cmp3.png (left before, right after), horizon zoom media/s38/hzcrop.png (before) vs hzcrop3.png (after). Brighter (0.6,0.75,0.85) hid it fully but washed the island out (cmp.png); darker (0.3,..) left a faint band (cmp2.png). Test tests/horizon.jl measures the ripple along the horizon row: 0.071 with the ground off (fails), passes (< 0.03) now. Frame median 1.8 ms (no per-frame cost). The worker restarts for the traced clips.

Waiting: a fidget every 7 s (preen under a wing, a peek at the sky, a foot tap, a feather shake); sad/bored: droops and taps its foot more; happy: sways. :proud: a chest-out hop with the legs along. plugins/birdbody.jl swaps the live herd once so the human's game got it at publish. - positions: creatures standing still do not move at all; moving creatures reverse direction (> 5 mm both frames) in 2/200 frames in one run, 137/1406 moving frames (10%) in another. Cumulus walking to its ring spot zigzagged (x 0.91, 0.97, 0.96, 1.02, 1.15, 1.10, 1.24 every 3 frames) = walking into a solid + Separation's radial push-out.
- a try: settling Separation's pushes in 4 passes per frame changed nothing (15% flips): reverted.
- yaw: reversals rare (3 in 200 frames), but single-frame snaps of 38-176 deg exist (sit/interact, eat/tend, sleep goal starts: a new goal sets yaw at once) and flight.jl look_at! sets yaw instantly.
- NOT yet checked: (1) the pose (species.jl pose_parts!: idle bob, fidgets, c.phase advancing while standing) between consecutive 1/24 s frames; (2) the clip camera: movies/flight.jl lerps S[:tgt] toward Lumi's position each frame, so the whole picture moves when Lumi moves (compare the background stones' pixel shift in the human's sheet with the sheep's: same shift = camera, different = creature); (3) whether frames in game_clip render the state BEFORE the shot callback moves the camera (one-frame lag alternating?).

The sheep in first-flight.mp4 was a flight WATCHER: suspects left = (a) the film camera (movies/flight.jl lerps S[:tgt] and S[:back] after Lumi every frame; any jerk in Lumi's position moves the whole picture), (b) the watcher walking into a solid at its ring spot and being pushed back out each frame (Cumulus zigzag measured), (c) flight.jl look_at! snapping yaw each frame while the engine turns it to its walk target. perfectionist-0082 [camera, high]: Jump-in starts with a round bush filling the middle of the view, Lumi half hidden behind it (jump-card.png). The leaf film is one static wide shot for 14 s, with a fence post filling the right third, jumpers 1/8 of the frame tall and Lumi at the far left edge. Live, the follow camera framed the dance ring from straight above Gloop's back, and during my leaf event it watched an empty pile while Lumi was off frame.
Where: greetings.jl chase_camera! start, plugins/autumn.jl leaves_view, movies/autumn.jl, render.jl circle groups
Suggestion: Start jump-in on open ground, or put the eye on the clear side with NG.obstruction. Film events the way an animator would: wide for the gust, then low close shots at the pile edge for each leap, and a medium shot of Lumi's run-up cutting to the burst. Keep group views below 30° pitch.
Done when: Five jump-in starts in a row show Lumi unobstructed (NG.obstruction < 1). The next event film's overview has >= 3 shots, with the jumper >= 1/3 of the frame height in one. The dance-ring pitch measured from game.rig is <= 32°.

items.detail: Host motion measure s76: Hopscotch (Crabbit) body and brows turn back 9x/s, Truffle (piglet) body and tail 8x/s (media/eyes/session-0076/motion.png: the crab's body rolls left/right every frame or two). Cause: species.jl body_pose(:walk/:run) rolls the body with sin(c.phase), and Crabbit's stride is 16 rad/m (speed 1.0, faster running), so the roll is 4-5 Hz. The pose does not know the species' gait rate. Ideas: pass a per-species body sway factor (Species field or a Dict by name) into pose_parts! and scale the roll by min(1, 6 / step rate); or roll with sin(c.phase / 2) for many-legged species. Also Cumulus (sheep, makeover.jl) leg_3/leg_4 jump 0.15-0.2 m in one frame at 1.3 s and leg_4 swings at 6.1 m/s: check the sheep's leg Step stride and pivot. Done when: live_motion() in the sandbox lists none of the three as vibrating or snapping.
items.result: Nobody shivers any more. Causes and fixes: (1) gait rates: plugins/gait.jl gives Crabbit 8 (was 16), Fluffkin 7 (12), Snootle 7 (10), Blorbo 9 (14) rad/m, with longer Steps for the sheep, piglet and blob legs (makeover.jl); (2) engine behavior.jl GAIT_MAX = 16 rad/s caps the gait cycle, so a tag chaser takes longer strides instead of rocking 12-14 times a second; (3) the piglet tail wag 0.35 rad at 1.8 (was 0.7 at 6, 11.6 m/s); (4) engine herd.jl pose blending: 0.22 s from the old action's pose to the new (Lumi's wing jumped 0.8-1.5 m in one frame at an action switch, now 0.2-0.27); (5) chats turn the pair to each other at 6 rad/s instead of a one-frame snap (behavior.jl face_each_other!). Evidence: live('motion') in the sandbox: before media/s76/motion-before (4 of 10 moving badly, vibrating 9-12/s), after media/s76/motion-cap3 (no vibrating; the only snaps are every creature jumping 0.15 m at the same instant 2.4 s, a sandbox frame hitch, not their motion). The first-play W/A/D tests, the flight test and the chat test pass. All published s76 (02:06-02:15), the human's game at 30 fps.

items.detail: Host motion measure s80: Lumi's beak jumped 1.08 m and its crest 1.00 m in one frame (body did not): a yaw snap, plugins set c.yaw outright in many places. Plan (s80, tried and reverted): smooth the DRAWN heading where the herd gets its data, scenery.jl sync! (motion = Vec3f(c.yaw, ...)): keep NG.DRAWN_YAW[c.id], turn it towards c.yaw at ~12 rad/s (no limit after dt > 0.5 s), pass it to the herd, and add NG.drawn_yaw(c); then use it in the four plugins that pose parts themselves (outfits.jl, egg.jl, paintfight.jl, sneeze.jl: NG.pose_parts!(..., c.yaw, ...)) or hats and the chick lead the body through every turn. A herd.jl-only version (POSE_MEMORY) would have done exactly that, so it was reverted. Batch with other engine edits. Done when: two live('motion') runs show no part of Lumi jumping > 0.15 m in one frame.
items.result: Engine scenery.jl: each creature's DRAWN heading (turn_drawn! in sync!, drawn_yaw(c)): changes up to 0.25 rad a frame pass straight through, a bigger one-frame jump (a plugin setting yaw outright) is eased at 12 rad/s, per creature object and world in weak dicts; outfits, sneeze and paintfight pose their parts with NG.drawn_yaw(c) so hats and paint turn with the body. A forced 180-degree turn of Lumi now takes ~0.2 s (drawn -0.51 -> 0.62 -> 1.93 -> 2.64 rad) instead of one frame. A/B with the DRAWN_ON switch, measured back to back: OFF 8, ON 7, OFF 9, ON 9 of 10 moving well (noise; the s81 first version that rate-limited every change measured 6/6/5 vs 10 and was reverted). Published s81 06:34, the human's game at 30 fps.
items.title: Turns that snap: Lumi's head swings a metre in one frame

At 09:57 in the sandbox 6 of 10 friends were 'asleep' like that, so the island looks like a freeze-frame of statues. The made-over bodies lost the old sleep pose with their old heads.
Where: plugins/makeover.jl bodies; species body_pose(:sleep) for Snootle/Crabbit; faces/outfits for closed eyes
Suggestion: A real sleep pose per made-over body: belly down (legs folded under, body lowered), head resting, lids closed (a lid piece over each eye), slow breathing on the body scale, an ear twitch or a Zz now and then. Pigs flop on their side, crabs tuck their claws in, sheep become a wool loaf. Also check why half the island naps mid-morning.
Done when: A close screenshot of a sleeping pig, crab, sheep and blob shows each lying down with closed eyes. In a 3 s motion strip the sleepers breathe (body scale changes) but their feet don't move.
Evidence: reviews/p91/pig-sleep.png (Pickles :sleep, standing, eyes open); reviews/p91/motion/creatures.png; eval at 09:57: Gloop, Wibbles, Pinchy, Cumulus, Marshmallow, Pickles all :sleep

perfectionist-0097 [fun, medium]: The stranger is the newest thing on the island, but a player who jumps in can do nothing with it: Lumi's visits and the friends' trust all run by themselves. 'Come and say hello?' asks the human to do something the game doesn't let them do. The scored games themselves are now polished. A first play wins with plenty to spare (hide and seek in 40 s of 120), but the levels give a second round a reason.

Evidence: plugins/stranger.jl (no keys_down or controlled player path)

items.detail: s92 and s93: two ffmpeg muxes inside Julia never ended (a looped picture + apad; then -c:v copy + amix + apad + -t), the first blocked the worker for half an hour, the second froze the sandbox for the rest of session 93 (a 100+ MB file growing, the sandbox cannot be shut down while the eval waits). Film scripts now write the silent film only (movies/visitors.jl); mix the sound in the agent's own shell with a timeout. Check movies/*.jl for other in-Julia ffmpeg muxes with apad and change them.
items.result:

items.detail: s96 tried it in lensclear.jl (each tree also counting a low skirt, 1.6 m ball at 1.9 m, and the real ~4 m crown, 2.1 m ball at 3.8 m): 10 follow shots went from 1-2 with a crown over a third of the view to none (media/s96/follow-before/sheet.png vs follow-after/sheet.png), but the test 'Follow camera: holds each creature at least 6 s and mostly sees faces' fell to 19 of 49 face samples (it passes without). Taken back. Next: count the crowns only near the eye (within ~4 m), or let the front view lift instead of swinging behind. The change is kept in /tmp only; redo from this note.
items.result: s96, second try: the low skirt (1.6 m ball at 1.9 m) and the real crown (2.1 m ball at 3.8 m) count only when their surface is within 3 m of the lens (lens_cost far = 3), so a crown right by the eye costs and front views past a tree stay free. All four 'Follow camera:' tests pass, including 'mostly sees faces' (it fell to 19/49 with the crowns counted at any distance). 10 follow shots 5 s apart: none with a crown over a third of the view (media/s96/follow-near/sheet.png; before: media/s96/follow-before/sheet.png had one under a dark crown over ~40%). Published.
items.title: Follow camera: out from under the tree crowns without losing the faces

items.detail:
perfectionist-0097 [creatures, high]: Shell stands on a jagged black plate (the generated image's baked shadow), in the raster and in the traced post still. It is one rigid mesh: it glides at 0.45 m/s with a constant |sin 7t| hop, its legs never step, its one big eye never turns, and its shell never sways. Next to the made-over crabs and pigs it reads as a figurine being dragged around.
Where: plugins/stranger.jl plots!/draw!, asset 20261125-195347-007-asset
Suggestion: Drop the plate faces (beach.jl trim_plate / makeover plate_mask). Cut the mesh like makeover.jl: feet that step, an eye stalk that turns towards whoever it watches, and a shell that lags and wobbles on a hop. Give it a waddle in place of the |sin| bounce, and a startled pull into its shell when someone shrieks. A thin-film or coat sheen on the shell for traced copies.
Done when: A close screenshot from the side shows no dark plate under Shell, and in live_motion's creature sheet Shell's feet and eye change between frames 0.4 s apart.
Evidence: reviews/perfectionist-shots/p97-shell.png (black plate under it, close up); site/img/stranger-ashore.png (dark patch at its feet)
items.result: s98: the generated image's baked shadow plate is gone (866 flat faces at the very bottom of Shell's mesh dropped in stranger.jl body_model, as beach.jl does): a side view on snow shows none (media/s98/shell-side.png). Shell no longer glides rigidly: while it walks it rolls 0.14 rad with its steps, nods and squashes 7% on each step (phase from the distance walked); standing it breathes and turns to look about. Not done: its legs and its eye cannot move on their own (one mesh; cutting it into parts like makeover.jl is the next step), and Shell is not a Creature, so live_motion does not measure it. Test passes; published.
items.title: Shell: a body that moves, without the black plate under it
